This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this repo is

`Taurus-Ai-Corp/Nexus` — the monorepo for **NEORM-ERA by Taurus AI**, plus
client work, campaign assets, and internal agent tooling. The site serves from
`nexus.taurusai.io` — a frozen infrastructure host; `neorm-era.com` is registered but still
on parking nameservers. It is a *workspace* monorepo, not a
single application: the shipping product surface is a small fraction of the tree.

Three things actually ship or run:

| Surface | Path | Stack |
|---|---|---|
| NEORM-ERA marketing site + serverless API | `platform/` | Static HTML/CSS/JS + Vercel functions (ESM, `type: module`) |
| Nexus backend API | `01-CORE-PLATFORM/nexus-backend/backend/` | FastAPI + SQLAlchemy async + Redis |
| Social suite dashboard | `social-suite-dashboard/` (git) / `06-AUTOMATION/social-suite-dashboard/` (disk) | Vite + Vitest, FastAPI api/ |

Everything else (`00-`…`10-` numbered dirs) is planning docs, client portals, marketing assets,
agent experiments, and archived material.

## Hooks that will act on your edits

`.claude/settings.json` wires three PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks. They are silent until they fire:

- **Writes to `.env` (not `.env.example`) and to any `docker-compose*.yml` are blocked.** Ask the
  user to make those changes; do not try to route around it.
- **Every `.py` file you Edit/Write is auto-`ruff format`ted afterwards.** Expect reformatting in
  your diff that you did not type.
- `.claude/hooks/edit-prevalidate.py` runs before every Edit/MultiEdit.

Root **`AGENTS.md` is generated** — it embeds a copy of this file under `## From CLAUDE.md` and is
rewritten automatically. Edit `CLAUDE.md`; never hand-edit `AGENTS.md`.

## Commands

### `platform/` — the shipping site (most common work)

```bash
cd platform
npm test                 # node --test on tests/*.test.js  — the real test suite
node --test tests/contact.test.js                                  # single file
node --test --test-name-pattern "security headers" tests/*.test.js  # single suite
npx serve . -p 3000      # preview the static site
```

### Backend — FastAPI

```bash
cd 01-CORE-PLATFORM/nexus-backend
python -m pytest backend/tests/ -q                        # the real tests (4 files)
python -m pytest backend/tests/test_tenancy_metering.py -q # single file
ruff check backend/services/ --config pyproject.toml       # lint a subtree you touched
cd backend && uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000        # run the API
```

**Lint the files you changed, never the tree.** `ruff check .` over `nexus-backend/` reports
**~10,500 errors** — the directory contains vendored external MCP servers, `subdomains/`, and
archived code that nothing excludes. Even `backend/` alone carries **63 pre-existing errors**
(B008, B904, F401, S607…). A clean run is not the baseline here; compare before/after on the
paths you edited, or just let pre-commit run ruff on staged files.

Backend tests import through `backend/services/__init__.py`, which imports
`vector_retrieval` → **numpy is a hard import even though `turbovec` is optional**. Needs
Python ≥3.11 (`datetime.UTC`, `X | None`). No working venv is checked in — `venv/` at repo root
is stale and lacks numpy/pytest, so create your own from `requirements.txt`.

### Docker

```bash
npm run docker:up        # postgres:5433, redis:6380, mongo:27017, n8n:5678
npm run docker:logs
```

Only those four start by default. `nexus-backend` and `agent-orchestrator` sit behind the
`full` profile and **both fail to build**: the backend build context points at
`nexus-backend/` whose `Dockerfile` runs `uvicorn main:app`, but `main.py` lives one level down
in `backend/`; and `02-AGENTS/orchestration/` is empty with no Dockerfile. Run the backend
directly (above) rather than via the `full` profile.

## Architecture: what needs multiple files to understand

### Backend billing core — `nexus-backend/backend/services/`

This is the most carefully designed part of the repo and the layer most recent commits touch.
Read the module docstrings; they carry the reasoning.

The pipeline is a fixed four-step contract, entered via `providers.generate_and_bill`:

```
resolve_credentials()  ->  ledger.open_job()  ->  await adapter.generate()  ->  ledger.close_job()
```

- **`tenancy.py`** answers one question per call: *whose key pays, and do we bill anyone?* It
  encodes the licensing boundary in code: **subscription-tier** providers (NotebookLM consumer,
  Google Flow, Higgsfield subscription) may not be resold to a paying client; **API-tier**
  (Gemini, Vertex Veo/Imagen) are resellable. Subscription-tier providers deliberately have **no
  adapter** in `services/providers/`. Credential values are never logged, repr'd, or returned in
  errors.
- **`metering.py`** records *both* `cost_cents` (what we paid the provider) and `billed_credits`
  (what the client paid). Storing only one makes margin permanently uncomputable. Credit price is
  set per **workflow**, not per model, so pricing survives a model swap.
- **`ledger_supabase.py`** is the durable async counterpart. The credit debit is a single
  conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= :n` so concurrent requests cannot both spend the last
  credit; `credits.balance` also carries a `CHECK (balance >= 0)`. Every method is `async` —
  a sync DB call here would serialise the whole FastAPI event loop.
  Schema: `05-DATABASES/supabase-migrations/migrations/0001_credits.sql`, `0002_generation_jobs.sql`.
- **`providers/rates.py`** — **no provider price is ever invented.** Every `ProviderRate` carries
  `verified_on=None` and the sentinel `cents_per_unit=Decimal("0")`, and jobs close with
  `cost_basis = CostBasis.UNVERIFIED`, until a human confirms a real rate. Never replace a
  sentinel with a plausible-looking number.

`services/vector_retrieval.py` is the turbovec-backed RAG layer; it degrades to empty results
when the native `turbovec` module is absent.

### Backend app wiring — `backend/main.py`

- `auth.py` is the **single source of truth** for JWT. `main.py` previously redefined
  `create_access_token`/`verify_token`/`hash_password`/`verify_password`, and the local copies
  silently won (24h token life instead of 15m, no `type` claim check). Those duplicates are
  deleted — do not reintroduce token helpers in `main.py`.
- `main.py` mutates `sys.path` (~line 50) to make `specialized.*` agents importable, so the
  imports below it are intentionally E402. Keep them there.
- Six specialized agents in `nexus-backend/agents/specialized/` are imported as classes. A
  seventh, `whatsapp_communication`, is owned by a separate workstream.

### `platform/` — static site with a hard function budget

Static pages at the root (`index.html`, `pricing.html`, …) with per-vertical landings in
`social/`, `creative/`, `intel/`, `freelance/`, `flow/`. `vercel.json` routes `/api/*` to
`platform/api/` and falls everything else through to `index.html`.

**`platform/api/` is at exactly 12 functions — the Vercel Hobby hard cap, with zero headroom.**
`tests/deploy-safety.test.js` enforces this. Adding a 13th `.js` file under `api/` breaks the
deploy; consolidate into an existing handler instead.

Shared campaign logic lives in `platform/lib/prompt-bible.mjs` (the 9-block campaign skeleton)
and is consumed by `api/campaign-pipeline.js`.

### Deploys drift ahead of the repo — this is why the guard tests exist

Every `nexus-platform` deploy is a **CLI deploy from a working tree**, so `git log` is *not* a
record of what is live. `tests/deploy-safety.test.js` documents two real regressions this caused:
`design-system.css` silently "restored" from an older snapshot (dropping nav-dropdown rules —
every page still returned 200, just unstyled), and six `campaigns/*.html` pages deleted locally
while still serving 200 in production. Treat those assertions as production invariants.

```bash
vercel --cwd platform --prod            # deploy the site
vercel --cwd platform --prod --force    # required when env vars or vercel.json change
```

`.claude/skills/deploy-nexus/SKILL.md` describes a 7-service Docker + Vercel deploy flow, but its
paths (`Nexus _ Platform Devops/`) no longer exist on disk — read it for the health-check matrix,
not for working commands.

## CI and pre-commit

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`: gitleaks → ESLint (`social-suite-dashboard/web/src/`, `--max-warnings 0`)
→ Ruff → Vite build → Vitest → pytest.

Two gaps worth knowing: the pytest job targets `nexus-backend/tests/` (the placeholder), so
**`backend/tests/` is not covered by CI**; and the Ruff job lints all of `nexus-backend/`, which
currently reports ~10,500 errors, so that job cannot pass as written. Do not assume a green CI
signal exists — run the backend tests yourself.

`.pre-commit-config.yaml`: brand guard → gitleaks → ruff `--fix` → eslint. Ruff is invoked from
the repo root with an explicit `--config`, which is why `pyproject.toml`'s per-file-ignore
patterns are globbed (`**/backend/auth.py`) — a bare relative path silently never matches.
Keep that glob form when adding entries.

The ruff per-file-ignores block is heavily commented and the comments are load-bearing: they
record which findings were genuinely *fixed* versus deliberately ignored, and why. Extend that
reasoning rather than adding bare ignores.

Media files (`*.mp4 *.mov *.avi *.webm *.gif`) are Git LFS-tracked.

```
platform/                 NEORM-ERA marketing site + Vercel serverless API  <- ships
01-CORE-PLATFORM/
  nexus-backend/backend/  FastAPI app: auth, services (tenancy/metering/ledger/providers)
  nexus-backend/agents/   specialized agents imported by main.py; MCP integrations
  nexus-studio/           Python content/agent workspace (NOT a Node package)
  nexus-creative/         Neormative CLI (TypeScript; directory name is frozen)
  brand-forge/            logo/mark generation + trademark search tooling
02-AGENTS/                agent registry, orchestration, creative agents
03-CLIENT-MANAGEMENT/     client portals (Mater Maria, YQG, EFS, TERA), CRM, research
04-CONTENT-MARKETING/     campaigns, leads, creative output, pricing intel
04-PRODUCT-DEPLOYMENT/    demos, proposals, presentations, legacy devops stack
05-DATABASES/             supabase-migrations/, plus supabase/mongo/planetscale schemas
06-AUTOMATION/            n8n workflows, social-suite-dashboard, partnerships
07-API-ROUTES/            standalone route/client modules (legacy naming)
08-DOCUMENTATION/         CLAUDE.md (canonical taxonomy + GWS/NotebookLM protocols), architecture, legal
09-ASSETS/ 10-CONFIG/     design assets; secrets config (SOPS — see .sops.yaml)
```

## Conventions

- Python: ruff with `select = ["E","F","I","N","W","UP","S","B"]`, line-length 100, double quotes.
- JS in `platform/`: ESM only (`"type": "module"`), `.mjs` for shared libs, Node's built-in
  test runner — no Jest/Vitest here.
- Secrets: SOPS-managed (`.sops.yaml`); `.env.example` documents the full variable surface
  (Supabase, PlanetScale, Mongo, Redis, HubSpot, SMTP/Brevo, Stripe, AI providers).
